name: Question 20
problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
K=[\begin{aligned}5 & -12 \\ 2 & -5\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $K=PD{P}^{-1},$ find $\operatorname{arctan}⁡K.$
worked_solution:
Given a function $f$ and matrices $A$ and $S,$ where $S$ is invertible, we have

$$
f(SA{S}^{-1})=S\cdot f(A)\cdot {S}^{-1}.
$$

For $f(x)=\operatorname{arctan}⁡K$ and the given matrix $K,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{arctan}⁡K=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(PD{P}^{-1})=P\cdot (\operatorname{arctan}⁡D)\cdot {P}^{-1}.
$$

Now, since $D$ is a diagonal matrix, we get

$$
\operatorname{arctan}⁡D=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{arctan}⁡1 & 0 \\ 0 & \operatorname{arctan}⁡(-1)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{4} & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{\pi }{4}\end{aligned}].
$$

Also, the inverse of $P$ is

$$
{P}^{-1}=\frac{3}{1\cdot 1-1\cdot 2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{arctan}⁡K & =P\cdot (\operatorname{arctan}⁡D)\cdot {P}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{4} & 0 \\ 0 & -\frac{\pi }{4}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{4} & -\frac{\pi }{2} \\ \frac{\pi }{4} & -\frac{3\pi }{4}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{5\pi }{4} & -3\pi  \\ \frac{\pi }{2} & -\frac{5\pi }{4}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the following matrices:

K=[5−122−5],D=[100−1],P=[3211]

Given that K=PDP−1, find arctan⁡K.

a
[π4−5π3π25π4]
b
[5π4−3ππ2−5π4]
c
[3π4−5ππ2−5π4]
d
[5π4−3π3π2π2]
e
[5π4−5ππ2−3π4]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Given a function f and matrices A and S, where S is invertible, we have f(SAS−1)=S⋅f(A)⋅S−1.

For f(x)=arctan⁡K and the given matrix K, we have

arctan⁡K=arctan⁡(PDP−1)=P⋅(arctan⁡D)⋅P−1.

Now, since D is a diagonal matrix, we get

arctan⁡D=[arctan⁡100arctan⁡(−1)]=[π400−π4].

Also, the inverse of P is

P−1=31⋅1−1⋅2[1−2−13]=[1−2−13].

Therefore, we conclude that

arctan⁡K=P⋅(arctan⁡D)⋅P−1=[3211][π400−π4][1−2−13]=[3211][π4−π2π4−3π4]=[5π4−3ππ2−5π4].
